title: Before the show had a name
summary: Ben Taylor proposed a late-night programme of records, live acoustic music, and poetry, with Maxie Haddow-Allen producing. Local performers could come from the Catweazle Club and the Union Bar. The possible slots were 1–3am on a Monday or Wednesday.
features: An Aztec Camera record every week, and a particularly long song every week.
‘Songs That Sound Better At The Wrong Speed’. We never did find a second song that sounded better at the wrong speed.
‘News from Pijnacker all the latest local gossip from this happening Dutch town’.
The French speaking clock, giving the wrong time.

title: Writing for the studio
summary: By January the opening had moved to four o’clock. Ben and Rufus had links between records. A poet and a musician each had time to come back for another piece. One jingle gives the show the mock announcement that it was filmed in front of a live studio audience.
features: Batman-style jingles for the time check, tea break, and phone-in. ‘dead air dead air dead air DEAD AIR!’
Record scratches, a whispered ident, and several versions of the same song to finish.

title: Eoin Quiery and the first Sunday
summary: The first running order puts ‘Teenage Kicks’ straight after the theme, then Television’s ‘Venus’ on vinyl. Eoin Quiery has three session slots. For Caroline Trettine’s ‘Be A Devil’, the operator is told to play thirty seconds at 45rpm, fade it, and start again at 33.
guests: Fraser – readings in the running order
evidence: A listener reported hearing the entire show on 20 February. Maxie later compared Eoin’s first-week session with Katie’s second-week one. These accounts establish both appearances; individual cues come from the running order.
features: Maxie’s trivia slot, with the Meco ‘Star Wars’ record underneath.
The wrong-speed record and the phone-in.

title: An extra half-hour
summary: With News Review off the schedule, the station offered us an extra half-hour. The revised sheet runs to 17:58. Superfly were booked to play ‘Short Skirts’, ‘Egg Beater Soul’, and ‘Circle-shaped’. Sam was to read, and the fishing phone-in would follow. The last record before the theme was to be Echo and the Bunnymen’s ‘The Killing Moon’.
evidence: In April Ben confirmed that Sam had done the demo and one show in the previous term. The 16 March sheet lists him as Sam.
features: ‘Is There Anybody Out There?’, Professor Pea, and the fishing phone-in.

title: Dylan, without mentioning Dylan
summary: The joke in Ben’s pitch was to spend the whole show on Dylan covers and originals without mentioning what they had in common. The dated song sheet gives Eoin Quiery ‘Tangled Up In Blue’ and ‘Simple Twist of Fate’, and George Kirby a ten-minute ‘Sad Eyed Lady of the Lowlands’. The companion script gives Dylan Bedford a poetry slot.
guests: Dylan Bedford – poetry in the script
evidence: The source is headed ‘Dead Air 8/6/97 – Songs’. The newspaper listing quoted that morning announced Ben and Rufus with music and poetry.
features: Professor P and the Boo Boys.

title: The farewell that was a week early
summary: Ben proposed a farewell show whose running joke was that the programme still had another week to go. The June 15 list brings back Jonathan Richman, adds Robert Wyatt’s ‘Shipbuilding’, and revisits the phone box outside the station. The date comes from the saved file and the sequence in Ben’s May pitch.

title: Christmas in June
summary: Our Christmas single was going to have me doing ‘Eternal Flame’ in the style of William Shatner, with Rufus Doors’ orchestral ‘Every Loser Wins’ on the other side. Sadly Rufus chose to leave town before the recording. On the morning of 22 June the station confirmed Dan Lester would operate the desk from 3 to 5 pm.
